head: Where to stay.
areas.intro: The coast you pick matters more than you'd think. On the east coast the tide goes out a long way, so the sea can be a walk away for part of the day. The north stays swimmable.

items.name: Kendwa
items.best: swimming at any time of day
items.line: A long, soft beach where the water stays deep close to shore. Sunsets over the sea.

items.name: Nungwi

items.line: Livelier, with more places to eat and dhows coming and going. Busy in parts, so where the hotel sits on the beach matters.

items.name: Matemwe and Pongwe

items.name: Paje and Jambiani

head: A week in Zanzibar.
week.intro: A sample plan to show how a trip can flow: two nights in Stone Town, then five on the beach. We shape it around your dates, your pace and your hotel.

Requests to the hotel, from a honeymoon set-up to a quiet room

days: Day 1
Arrive and slow down
Land and transfer to your Stone Town hotel, a short drive away.
Freshen up, pray and rest.
Walk to Forodhani Gardens near sunset for the evening food stalls by the water.
Day 2
Stone Town on foot
A morning walk with a private guide: the Old Fort, the carved doors and the narrow lanes.
Darajani Market for spices, fruit and the morning bustle.
An afternoon boat to Prison Island to see the giant tortoises.
Maghrib by the sea, then dinner in town.
Day 3
Spices, forest, then the coast
A spice farm tour on the way out of town: cloves, cinnamon, vanilla and fresh fruit.
Jozani Forest to see the red colobus monkeys.
Check in at your beach hotel in the afternoon.
Day 4
Nothing planned
Breakfast, the pool, the beach. That's the plan.
On the east coast, check the tide times and swim at high water.
A quiet dinner, or an early night.
Day 5
Out on the water
A snorkelling trip to Mnemba Atoll, where you may see dolphins on the way out.
Or a dhow day with a sandbank stop and lunch on the boat.
Day 6
Your choice
A sunset dhow cruise, a spa afternoon or a first kitesurfing lesson in Paje.
If it's a Friday, ask us about Jumu'ah near your hotel.
Day 7
Last full day
A slow morning, a long lunch and one more swim.
Pick up spices or a kanga cloth to take home.
Day 8
Home
We can ask the hotel for a late check-out.
Allow about an hour or more to reach the airport from the north and east coasts.

head: Before you go.
tips.intro: The practical bits, in one place.
items: flights
Getting there
There are no direct flights from Manchester. Most routes change once, in Doha, Dubai, Muscat or Istanbul.
The airport is just outside Stone Town. Transfers to the north and east coasts take about an hour or more.
shield
Visa and insurance
British passport holders need a visa. The e-visa is the easiest way: apply online before you fly.
Your passport needs at least six months left from the day you arrive, and a blank page.

If you land in Zanzibar first, you also need the government's inbound travel insurance from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation, even if you have your own policy. Buy it only from the official site, visitzanzibar.go.tz.
Rules change, so check GOV.UK before you travel.
fee
Money
The local currency is the Tanzanian shilling.
Hotels, transfers and trips are often priced in US dollars.
Keep some small notes for markets, tips and taxis.
beach
Weather
June to October is dry, sunny and a little cooler.
December to February is hot and humid, and it's the busiest time.
The long rains fall in April and May, when some hotels close. Shorter rains come around November.
pray
Prayer and Ramadan
There are masjids across Stone Town and in the villages. Ask your hotel for the qibla and a prayer mat, or we can request one before you arrive.
In Ramadan, many cafes and restaurants outside hotels close in the day and open after sunset. Hotels serve guests as normal.
Ramadan 2027 is expected to begin around 8 February, depending on the moon sighting.
people
Dress and manners
Modest dress is expected in Stone Town and the villages, for men and women.
Keep swimwear for the beach and the pool.
A few words go a long way: jambo (hello), asante (thank you), karibu (welcome).
tips.foot: Entry details checked against GOV.UK travel advice on 21 November 2026. Rules, prices and opening times change.

head: Questions.
items: Is Zanzibar good for a Muslim honeymoon?

For many couples, yes. It's a mostly Muslim island with quiet villas, private pools and long beaches. Many resorts serve alcohol and cater to international guests, so we check each hotel and tell you plainly what to expect.
Is the food halal?
Most people on the island are Muslim, but resorts cater to international guests, so it's best not to assume. We ask each hotel about its meat and kitchens before you book and tell you what we find.
Which side of the island should we stay on?

If you want to swim whenever you like, the north: Kendwa or Nungwi. If you'd rather have quiet, wide beaches and don't mind planning around the tide, the east. Splitting your stay between the two works well.
What do we need before we fly?
A visa (the e-visa is easiest), a passport with at least six months left, and Zanzibar's government travel insurance if you land there first. Rules change, so check GOV.UK before you travel.
Can we add another stop?
Yes. Stone Town and a beach is the classic pairing, and a stopover in Doha or Dubai works well on the way. Tell us what you have in mind.

FAQ_Q1: Why use Saphara instead of booking it myself?

You can book it yourself. What we add is the part booking sites don't do: we compare a few hotels we'd book ourselves, ask the hotel for your requests and get them confirmed, and stay on WhatsApp while you're away. There's no service fee for any of it.
Can you beat a price I've found?

Sometimes, not always. Send us the hotel and the price and we'll compare it like for like: the same room, board basis, cancellation terms and extras. If we can get a better rate, we'll tell you. If we can't, we'll tell you that too.
Do you charge a fee?
No. We don't charge a service fee, and the price we quote is the price you pay, with no hidden fees.
How do you make money if there's no service fee?
The rates we get from hotels and suppliers include our margin, so you pay the price we quote and nothing extra.
Are the hotels you recommend halal?

We don't call a hotel halal unless we've checked. A resort in a Muslim-majority country isn't automatically halal, so for each hotel we look at the kitchen, whether alcohol is served, the beach and pools, and prayer space. Then we tell you plainly.
